explanation: Mixed: fires on function words and verbs in non-English Romance/Scandinavian sentences (Romanian 'cred', French 'en', Norwegian 'å', Swedish 'inte', Danish 'at') and also on word-internal fragments of proper nouns and technical terms (Vander[La]an, [Pro]vo, R-[W]is., [conf]ocal, NI[AG]RA). Common English function words in ordinary prose give little or no activation.

Fires on words expressing persistence or continuation of a state: 'remain', 'still', 'retain', 'keep', 'stay intact', 'continue (to)', and the token right after such a verb (e.g. 'the' in 'must retain the above copyright'). Strongest after modals like 'will/can' + still/remain; weak for unrelated content.

Fires on characters inside random-looking alphanumeric strings: hashes, password hashes, URL slugs/IDs (pic.twitter.com/..., youtube watch?v=, jsfiddle IDs), tokens and keys. The token is a single letter/digit chunk in a mixed-case, meaningless string; ordinary words fire weakly at most.

Diffuse: fires on assorted connective/quantifier tokens (every, all, any, not in 'but are not limited to', 'where', 'per', 'to' in ranges like '12 to 25'), commas, and indentation whitespace in code. No single context predicts it well.

Fires on the head or second part of technical terms in programming/science/legal contexts (get_[where], fail[over], search and [sort], create a [table], quantum [Hall], top[ological], denial of [Service], emotional dist[ress]). Loosely 'completing a domain-specific term'; plain narrative words are weak.

Fires on word-internal subword pieces of technical compounds and abbreviations, strongest for 'frame(s)' in CSS/HTML (@key[frames], i[Frame]), then biomedical word pieces (germ-[free], cyt[oker]atin, phot[oper]iod, neuro[f]ibrillary) and letters in acronyms (IRF4, GCTF). Whole common words do not fire.

Mainly chemistry/materials text: fires on tokens within chemical names and lists (the '(' before a formula after 'selenite', 'with calcium', 'lithium', 'aluminum', 'acids,', 'glass ionomer'). Separately fires on the first digit '0' of a year in copyright headers ('Copyright (c) 2[0]12').

Diffuse: fires on 'of' in partitive phrases ('one of', 'some of', 'out of'), intensifiers like 'much', indentation whitespace and constructors in code ('new', 'Thread'), and assorted grammatical tokens. Hard to predict from a single rule.

Fires on CSS class names inside HTML class attributes or CSS/jQuery selectors (class="weui-cell we[ui]...", 'col-md', '.form-control', '.tab', 'pull-right'), especially the second or later class in a list. Near zero outside markup/style code.

Fires on the first subword fragment of a rare or multi-token word, often a proper noun, place name, or biological term ([W]istar, [mam]mary, [Cor]vallis, [Cam]bridgeshire, [Tri]este, [E]czema, Ha[em]agogus), where the model must predict the rest of the word. Complete common words fire weakly.

Mixed: strongest on 'someone/anybody' in help requests ('Can someone explain/help'), on 'own' in 'by his own admission', and on person-related nouns (user, listener, public); also fires on the space before an age after a person's name in news ('Brittany Peoples, 20') and 'of' in 'Olympic cyclists of Italy' category lines.

Mixed: fires on 'ography' in 'bibliography:' YAML front matter, suffix pieces completing technical words (octah[edral], transesophage[al], Chi-s[quared]), '=' in static field initializers, method calls like '.close', and assorted words (residue, fleeing, World [War]). No unified trigger.

Fires weakly-to-moderately on scattered word fragments in foreign-language words and names (s[ambil], D[apat], Y[ous]afzai, Fl[ugh]afen, atro[ven]etum) plus random tokens in code and lists; the one strong example is Malay slang. No clear pattern.

Fires on tokens in formatted boilerplate headers: court-document captions with heavy whitespace (UNITED STATES, IN THE, clerk names' initials) and code namespace/package identifiers (NHapi[.Base], Mage_Sales, www[.boost]), plus indented code tokens. Roughly 'header/identifier tokens after long whitespace runs', but mixed.
